purpose: Single synthetic live discussion; not a benchmark or a physical test

brief.input: recycled rubber pieces with a characterized binder stock
brief.targets: wet grip and durability matter; test methods and limits are not yet known
brief.variation: the rubber mass fraction of an incoming portion can differ
brief.available_changes: explore a characterized binder addition and test the new mix

request.question: Help interpret this synthetic composition calculation for setup Synthetic mat setup, ID synthetic-setup, version 1. The entered portion is one kilogram with 26 mass percent recycled rubber. The added characterized binder contains zero percent recycled rubber. A user chooses a trial composition of 20 percent. The deterministic calculation gives 0.3 kilograms of binder, assuming no losses. What practical next checks and limitations matter? Do not treat this as a tested recipe or predict grip or durability.

questions.question: What is this stock's amount and quantity basis? Unknown context can remain captured.
Which relevant specimen/product geometry or installation conditions describe it?
Which property checks are required for this product? No required checks cannot establish an all-check result.

warnings: This assessment describes entered readings only; no interpolation, causal effect, future-batch consistency or finished-product qualification is established.

response.answer:
Save the 0.3 kg as arithmetic for that 1 kg portion only. It moves 0.26 kg rubber to 20% if nothing is lost. It does not show grip, durability, or what another portion needs.

Use it only if that portion is really 26% rubber from a stated measurement or reliable feed record. Reweighing or splitting the pile alone does not give the rubber share. Your captured setup still has unknown making conditions and no test-piece shape, so keep the earlier setup and save any binder mix as a changed version.

A made piece still needs its own wet-grip and durability checks. The number alone does not qualify the mat and does not carry to other incoming portions.
next_steps: Confirm how the 26% rubber share was set for this 1-kg portion before using the 0.3-kg figure.
Check scale suitability and record start and finish masses to see losses when you prepare the changed version.
Make and test the changed version separately for wet grip and durability; do not carry the result to other portions.
questions: What measurement or record gives the 26% rubber share for this portion?
What binder stock, test-piece shape and making conditions will you use for the new mix?
Which wet-grip and durability checks are required for this mat and installation?

sources.title: HSE — assessing floor slip resistance
sources.scope: General floor-slip testing guidance, including instrumented pendulum assessment by a suitably trained operator under relevant surface conditions. It supplies no measured slip value, acceptance target or qualification for the user's recycled material, and no home walking test substitutes for it. Check the current applicable method for the product and installation.

sources.title: Cecon 2021 — measured recycled-PE blends
sources.scope: The study's PE blends and injection process only. It illustrates measuring a response at separate recycled-content levels, not a density or recipe for another material.

sources.title: NIST — weighing and scales FAQs
sources.scope: General weighing/tare guidance supports weighing the complete assembly including its enclosure. Scale capability and measurement uncertainty must suit the target tolerance; display resolution alone does not establish accuracy. This does not establish enclosure strength, fill retention or product qualification.
